title: Migration 3 — security hardening: search_path pinning and grant narrowing (apply-only)
description: Applies migration 3 on a disposable PostgreSQL 17 cluster. This migration ships NO ROLLBACK file, so reversibility cannot be proven and is not claimed: the fixture covers what is provable — that 3 applies cleanly against a real cluster on the major production runs. It existed outside the harness's old *_HARDENING.sql denominator (defect D6), so before this fixture a fully green run said nothing whatever about it while looking identical to one that covered it. The absence of a rollback is printed on every run rather than left to be inferred from a silence. A PRE-21-WORLD stage is required because the substrate is modelled on current production, which carries migration 21's hardened handle_new_user(), and migration 3 REFUSES to run against it — re-running 3 would revert that function to the 'farmer' default and re-open anonymous self-provisioning. Migration 3 predates 21, so a genuine pre-3 world is at least a pre-21 one; the existing pre-21 stage is reused rather than duplicated.
